column7: Outdoor cushions¶The covers are 100% olefin, an outdoor fabric made to resist water and fading. Deal with a spill or stain as soon as it happens: work in a little mild soap and lukewarm water with a soft-bristled brush, rinse until no soap is left, and let the cushions dry in the open air. Washing by hand is gentler than a machine and helps the cushions last longer. Keep bleach and fabric softener away from them. After rain, stand cushions on edge so the water drains, and bring them in or store them somewhere dry through the off season.¶¶Teak frame¶The frame is teak with a grey-washed, water-based finish. Teak's natural oils let it live outdoors; over time sun and rain soften the finish, and the wood moves gradually toward its own silver-grey, which sits easily with the washed tone. To clean, wash with mild soapy water and a soft brush, rinse and let it dry. Never use a pressure washer, which raises the grain. A teak protector or sealer is optional, never required; try it first on a hidden spot, since some products warm the colour.¶¶Glides¶Check the plastic glides now and then and keep them clean of grit, so the piece slides without marking deck boards, stone or tile.¶¶Seasonal storage¶In harsh winter weather, cover the piece with a breathable cover or store it somewhere dry and airy. Bring cushions indoors for the off season.¶¶A Note on Natural Variation¶Teak is a natural material, and grain, tone and small knots vary from board to board and piece to piece. As it weathers, colour shifts gradually; this is part of the character of the wood.

column7: Outdoor cushions¶The covers are 100% olefin, an outdoor fabric made to resist water and fading. Deal with a spill or stain as soon as it happens: work in a little mild soap and lukewarm water with a soft-bristled brush, rinse until no soap is left, and let the cushions dry in the open air. Washing by hand is gentler than a machine and helps the cushions last longer. Keep bleach and fabric softener away from them. After rain, stand cushions on edge so the water drains, and bring them in or store them somewhere dry through the off season.¶¶Teak frame¶The frame is teak with a grey-washed, water-based finish. Teak's natural oils let it live outdoors; over time sun and rain soften the finish, and the wood moves gradually toward its own silver-grey, which sits easily with the washed tone. To clean, wash with mild soapy water and a soft brush, rinse and let it dry. Never use a pressure washer, which raises the grain. A teak protector or sealer is optional, never required; try it first on a hidden spot, since some products warm the colour.¶¶Glides¶Check the plastic glides now and then and keep them clean of grit, so the piece slides without marking deck boards, stone or tile.¶¶Seasonal storage¶In harsh winter weather, cover the piece with a breathable cover or store it somewhere dry and airy. Bring cushions indoors for the off season.¶¶A Note on Natural Variation¶Teak is a natural material, and grain, tone and small knots vary from board to board and piece to piece. As it weathers, colour shifts gradually; this is part of the character of the wood.

Name changed from the first draft, Orrefors, because it is a live glass brand, and then from Murano, because it is a protected glass origin name.¶Line 1 of the name is BH | Studio (indoor), not BH | Outdoor.¶Colour: white opaque glass shade, black metal base as Jet (house rule: black metal is Jet), checked on the full-size photo.¶Bulb not included per the vendor; G45 E26, 60W maximum, LED compatible.
column6: Materials: Opaque White glass globe shade on a Jet iron cone base; black power cord with inline on/off switch; takes one G45 E26 bulb, 60W maximum, or an LED equivalent (bulb not included); compatible with a dimmer switch (not included); assembly required; single table lamp.¶¶Product dimensions: Height 16 in, Width 6 in, Depth 6 in¶¶Shade: Height 6 in, Width 6 in, Depth 6 in¶¶Base: Width 4 in, Depth 4 in¶¶Weight: TBD.¶¶Boxed dimensions: TBD.
column7: Glass shade¶Switch the lamp off, unplug it and let the bulb cool before cleaning. Dust the globe with a soft, dry cloth; for marks, use a cloth wrung out in plain water, then dry the glass straight away. Never use abrasive cleaners.¶¶Metal base¶Wipe clean using a cloth wrung out in water, then dry at once. Avoid abrasive pads and harsh chemicals, which can dull the finish.¶¶Bulb and cord¶Use one G45 E26 bulb of 60W or less, or an LED equivalent; an LED runs cooler inside the globe. Keep the cord clear of walkways and never run it under a rug.
